questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your whole body. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see.
Avoid placing you in other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Provide you with an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and should give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and your shoulders to get a better look.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Only move your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Feel free to talk whenever they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel free to talk whenever they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move unnecessarily so the rider can focus. Passengers should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the rider and hold firmly to the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle and trying to turn, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle as that can be unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than a walk, your motorcycle needs to lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn. This causes the motorcycle to lean the right way.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best riding formation is generally:

options.text: Pairs.
A staggered formation.
A single-file line.
A pyramid formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: To increase your chances of being seen at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride with your headlight on.
Reduce your space cushion.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on to be more visible at intersections. Ride in a lane position that helps oncoming traffic see you. Keep a space cushion so you can avoid danger. Do not assume other drivers see you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: When being passed, you should not move to the portion of the lane farthest from the passing driver because it:

options.text: Discourages the passing driver from cutting into your lane too early.
Encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
Encourages the passing driver to complete the pass as quickly as possible.
Encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourages the passing driver to cut into your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane when being passed is dangerous. It may make the passing driver cut back into your lane too early. It is safest to stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs show road rules, such as speed limits. These signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The center of the lane
The right side of the lane
There is no single best position for all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position for all situations.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or always bad. Choose a position based on current conditions. Make sure you have enough space and other drivers can see you.

questions.question: Why should you not ride too far to the right when riding a three-wheeled motorcycle or with a sidecar?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side. If you ride too far right, the sidecar may go off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel may leave the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group
Just behind the leader
Near the back of the group
At the very end of the group

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they do not have to chase the group. Experienced riders behind them can watch and help them.

questions.question: For an eye or face shield to work well, it must:

options.text: Fasten securely
Block all air from passing through
Not allow room for eyeglasses
Block your side vision

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must fasten securely. It should be scratch-free and hard to break. It should allow clear views to the sides and let air pass through to prevent fogging. It should also fit eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: To carry a passenger safely, you may need to adjust:

options.text: The shocks
The handlebars
The brakes
The throttle

questions.correctAnswerText: The shocks
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight. You may need to adjust the shocks before carrying a passenger. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: If road conditions need a longer stopping distance, you should:

options.text: Decrease your following distance
Increase your following distance
Travel on the shoulder
Ask someone else to ride your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle needs more time to stop, keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead. Use at least a three-second following distance when the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When it is raining, you should usually:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane
Pull off the road until the rain stops
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
Speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the road is very slippery. Oil from cars has not washed away yet. Riding in tire tracks left by cars is safest. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from everything except:

options.text: Sunburn
Windburn
Chapped lips
Dehydration

questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Good clothes also protect you if you crash.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes
Squeeze the front brake hard to prevent the tire from locking
Use only the rear brake
Use one brake at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Never use a staggered formation
Place inexperienced riders at the back
Not use your mirrors
Not ride too close to other riders

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride too close to other riders
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. Check your mirrors often. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep proper space between all riders.

questions.question: Debris and oil drippings collect in which part of a traffic lane?

options.text: The center of the lane
Where motorcycle riders should always travel
Where most accidents happen
Where drivers are least likely to see a motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane
questions.explanation: Debris and oil drippings from cars collect in the center of the lane. Other hazards like utility hole covers are also found there.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist prevent other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane
Ride in the center portion of the lane
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into your lane
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left position
The center position
The right position
There is no single best position

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position
questions.explanation: No single position is always best. Change your lane position as conditions change. Choose a position that gives you the most space and makes it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: What formation should a group of riders use when entering a curve?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use a single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. A staggered formation works best on straightaways while keeping adequate spacing.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When approaching a police officer
When someone is following too closely
When there is a stop sign ahead
When your signals are not working

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is following too closely. This warns the driver behind you that you are slowing down. Also flash your brake light when you slow down in a place where drivers might not expect it.
